Join us at KAI and become a key player in the semiconductor industry, where every design and test brings us closer to a sustainable, electrified future! Master's / PhD in Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

Strong expertise in SPICE and system-level simulations of power electronic circuits

Proven experience in PCB design using industry-standard tools like ALTIUM Designer

Practical experience with power electronic hardware design, from concept to laboratory validation

Excellent communication skills in English and/or German

The ability to lead and mentor junior team members, fostering a collaborative and innovative workspace

jobs.occupation: Senior Partner Development Manager – Distribution Partners Germany, EMEA Partner Organization (Betriebswirt/in - allgemeine Betriebswirtschaft)
jobs.employer_name: Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL Niederlassung Deutschland
jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking an experienced Distribution Partner Development Manager to own and drive the AWS distribution strategy across Germany. In this role, you will manage and grow strategic relationships with our Authorised Distribution Partners such as Ingram Micro and TD Synnex, particularly for SMB and Enterprise customers. An additional area of responsibility is to grow the business with large value added resellers (“Systemhäuser”, e.g. Bechtle, Cancom) across Enterprise and Public Sector Accounts.

The AWS Distribution Program enables our distributors to act as force multipliers — leveraging their deep partner relationships, market knowledge, and specialised expertise to extend the reach of AWS solutions to customers we cannot efficiently serve through direct channels alone. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role that requires a rare blend of strategic thinking, commercial acumen, and operational discipline. You will not only execute on strategy — you will shape it, acting as the voice of distribution into AWS program design discussions and influencing worldwide policy decisions where distribution-specific considerations are required.

As the single-threaded owner of the German distribution channel, you will serve as the primary interface between AWS and our distributors, driving incremental revenue through their reseller communities. You will work cross-functionally with AWS sales, partner, marketing, and solutions architecture teams to accelerate cloud adoption at scale, particularly within the SMB Commercial Sector.

Key job responsibilities
Partner Management & Strategy
• Own end-to-end relationships with Authorised Distribution and Systemhaus Partners in Germany.
• Develop and execute joint business plans aligned to AWS go-to-market and EMEA strategy.
• Drive QBRs and cadence meetings with partner leadership at VP/CXO level.
• Grow distributor-attributed and AWS Marketplace revenue YoY.
• Pursue new routes-to-market and "Power of Three" collaboration.

Revenue & Performance Management
• Own revenue targets for the German channel, including resell and influenced revenue.
• Monitor distributor performance: revenue, recruitment, enablement, pipeline.
• Produce monthly partner reports from internal dashboards.
• Analyse trends, flag risks/opportunities, drive action plans.
• Track Partner Attributed Revenue and ensure accurate attribution.

Program Design & Execution
• Act as the voice of distribution into AWS program design discussions, representing field-level feedback on attribution models, incentive structures, and partner programs.
.
• Ensure distributors are enabled on launches and policy changes.

Enablement & Ecosystem Growth
• Recruit, onboard, and activate new resellers into the channel.
• Align with PDMs and Account Managers across direct, distribution, and "Power of Three" motions.
• Drive technical enablement (AI, Migration, Data & Analytics); support co-sell/co-marketing.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Align Germany execution with EMEA Scale & Distribution strategy.
• Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Partner Solutions Architects, Operations.

About the team
The Distribution team sits within the Amazon Partner Organisation in Germany & Europe Central, focused on extending AWS's reach through established distributor communities to serve the Commercial Sector at scale. You'll be part of a collaborative, high-performing team that values customer obsession, partner obsession, and execution excellence.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience developing strategies that influence leadership decisions at the organizational level
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences
- Minimum 6 years of channel experience, with specific distribution, indirect channel or reselling background
- German and English business fluent
- Cloud and/or digital transformation experience — understanding of cloud business models, consumption economics, and partner ecosystems
- Proven ability to manage breadth over depth — portfolio management across 30+ partners through leverage and prioritisation
- Strong commercial acumen: pipeline management, forecasting, and revenue accountability
- Demonstrated stakeholder management across complex, matrixed organisations

Preferred Qualifications

- Direct experience with IT distribution (Ingram Micro, TD SYNNEX, Arrow, ALSO) or Systemhaus channel (Bechtle, Cancom, Computacenter)
- AWS or hyperscaler partner programme experience
- Experience with CRM systems and pipeline analytics (Salesforce preferred)
- Understanding of software marketplace transaction models and cloud procurement
- Track record of building new coverage models or channel motions from scratch
- Familiarity with German SMB and mid-market IT landscape

Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build.

Our tax team of six, led by our Head of Tax, covers the tax matters of all group companies worldwide. To support us in Berlin or Karlsruhe, we are looking for a Tax Specialist (f/m/d)  who wants to work across the full range of our tax topics and is keen to build expertise in transfer pricing.

Tasks

- Preparing tax balance sheets and tax returns for the German group companies together with our colleagues.
- Support in preparing and maintaining our transfer pricing documentation (Master File, Local Files, CbCR), including functional and risk analyses.
- Contributing to the implementation and further development of intercompany transfer pricing guidelines and models and reviewing intercompany agreements in coordination with the business functions.
- Tax assessment of business transactions, contracts and restructurings.
- Advising business functions and subsidiaries on tax matters, and acting as contact person for our foreign entities on operational questions regarding the operational application of transfer pricing requirements.
- Supporting tax audits and communicating with tax authorities and external advisors.
- Helping us develop our Tax Compliance Management System further and digitalise our tax processes.
- Monitoring legislative changes and case law, and deriving recommendations for action.

Qualifications

- Academic track record with a finance and international tax background.
- At least three years of professional experience in tax consultancy, audit, or an in-house tax function; experience in the tax department of a multinational group is an advantage.
- German Tax Advisor Exam is an advantage.
- Sound knowledge of German corporate income tax law; knowledge of international tax law is desirable.
- Initial exposure to transfer pricing, or a clear interest in building expertise in this area.
- Experience with SAP and common tax software, along with very good Excel skills.
- Structured and independent way of working, and enjoyment of working with different business functions.
- Business-fluent German and good English language skills.

Benefits

- Hybrid working model.
- Flexible working hours through trust-based working hours.
- At some locations a subsidized canteen and various free drinks.
- Modern office space with very good transport connections.
- Various employee discounts for activities and products.
- Employee events such as summer and winter parties, as well as workshops.
- Numerous training and development opportunities.
- Various health offers, such as sports and health courses.

jobs.occupation: Earth Observation (EO) & Remote Sensing Engineer (m/f/d) (Data Scientist)
jobs.description:
Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:
Remote Sensing Specialists; Data Scientists; Physicists

Stellenbeschreibung:
Earth Observation (EO) & Remote Sensing Engineer (m/f/d) 

Location: Germany (Hybrid / Remote options available)  

Contract Type: Full-Time Employment (Permanent)  

Target Group: Remote Sensing Specialists, Data Scientists, Physicists, Opportunity Card Holders, and Master's Graduates  

About Project IRIS Project IRIS develops AI-supported spatial resilience and geospatial data models for the energy transition. To breathe dynamic life into our static infrastructure data, we integrate global earth observation data into our central inference engine. In this role, you will add the dimension of real-time surface activity and physical states to our spatial intelligence models. 

Your Focus & Responsibilities 

- Satellite Pipelines: Build automated pipelines to fetch and process Sentinel-1 (Radar/InSAR) and Sentinel-2 (Multispectral) data via the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. 
- Algorithm Development: Develop algorithms to automatically detect surface changes, vegetation decline, moisture indices (NDVI/NDWI), and thermal anomalies. 
- Data Integration: Seamlessly integrate derived raster metadata and Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG) into our central PostGIS vector database. 

What We Are Looking For 

- Technical Background: Degree in Remote Sensing, Geoinformatics, Data Science, Physics, or equivalent practical industry experience.  
- Core Technical Skills: Deep practical experience in processing satellite data (Landsat, Sentinel) using Python libraries such as Rasterio, xarray, or GDAL. 
- Mindset: An analytical mindset capable of deriving tangible ecological, thermal, and structural factors from raw pixel values. 
- Eligibility: Open to local applicants and international candidates (Chancenkarte / Opportunity Card supported).  
- Languages: Professional working proficiency in English (required); German language skills are a plus.  

What We Offer 

- Full-Time Permanent Employment: Long-term career stability with clear growth trajectories.  
- Dual Master / Trainee Track Available: Tailored tracks including academic coordination and complete tuition support.  
- Accommodation & Onboarding Package: Structured assistance with local accommodation, official registration, and comprehensive onboarding.  
- Visa & Administrative Backing: Dedicated employer support for Opportunity Card conversions and visa applications.  
- Modern Tech Environment: Work in a high-efficiency environment focused on cutting-edge geospatial intelligence.  

How to Apply: Send your CV by E-Mail:  

jobs-geo@iris-institut.org (Subject: Application - Earth Observation Engineer)

jobs.occupation: Big Data & Backend Engineer – Spatial ETL (m/f/d) (Data Engineer)
jobs.description:
Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:
Backend Engineers; Data Engineers; Database Administrators

Stellenbeschreibung:
Big Data & Backend Engineer – Spatial ETL (m/f/d) 

Location: Germany (Hybrid / Remote options available)  

Contract Type: Full-Time Employment (Permanent)  

Target Group: Backend Engineers, Data Engineers, Database Administrators, Opportunity Card Holders, and Master's Graduates  

About Project IRIS Project IRIS is a proprietary applied research initiative processing massive amounts of infrastructure and spatial data. We bridge the gap between fragmented public data and actionable infrastructure intelligence. When standard APIs reach their limits and entire national registries must be processed, you step in. In this role, you are the architect for heavy data loads and robust backend pipelines.  

Your Focus & Responsibilities 

- Bulk Processing: Automate the download and processing of massive data dumps (e.g., corporate registers, industrial emission databases like PRTR, energy grids). 
- ETL Engineering: Program high-performance ETL pipelines that decompress, parse, and transfer complex archives into our central PostgreSQL architecture. 
- Database Governance: Ensure idempotency, deduplication, and reliable monitoring during weekly multi-million row updates. 
- Container Orchestration: Deploy and maintain isolated Docker environments for all ingestion tasks.  

What We Are Looking For 

- Technical Background: Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or extensive practical backend industry experience.  
- Core Technical Skills: Expertise in processing relational mass data, strong Python skills (SQLAlchemy, Pandas), and deep PostgreSQL performance tuning. 
- Mindset: A clean-code engineering approach focused on system stability and scalability.  
- Eligibility: Open to local applicants and international candidates (Chancenkarte / Opportunity Card supported).  
- Languages: Professional working proficiency in English (required); German language skills are a plus.  

What We Offer 

- Full-Time Permanent Employment: Long-term career stability with clear growth trajectories.  
- Dual Master / Trainee Track Available: Tailored tracks including academic coordination and complete tuition support.  
- Accommodation & Onboarding Package: Structured assistance with local accommodation, official registration, and comprehensive onboarding.  
- Visa & Administrative Backing: Dedicated employer support for Opportunity Card conversions and visa applications.  
- Modern Tech Environment: Work in a high-efficiency environment centered on Python, PostGIS, and Docker.

jobs-trainee@iris-institut.org (Subject: Application - Big Data & Backend Engineer)

jobs.occupation: Municipal Data Mining & OParl Specialist (m/f/d) (Data Engineer)
jobs.description:
Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:
Software Engineers; NLP Specialists; Data Miners

Stellenbeschreibung:
Municipal Data Mining & OParl Specialist (m/f/d) 

Location: Germany (Hybrid / Remote options available)  

Contract Type: Full-Time Employment (Permanent)  

Target Group: Software Engineers, NLP Specialists, Data Miners, Opportunity Card Holders, and Master's Graduates  

About Project IRIS Project IRIS is an applied research initiative capturing and analyzing large volumes of public, unstructured text data from municipal information systems. By tracking local planning decisions before they hit official cadastral portals, we create early-warning systems for infrastructure development. In this role, you will build the automated agents that read and understand municipal government data. 

Your Focus & Responsibilities 

- API Integration: Develop and maintain Python-based interfaces to autonomously query municipal council information systems, primarily using the open OParl standard. 
- Document Parsing: Parse and structure extensive text documents, meeting minutes, and official zoning announcements (PDFs, HTML). 
- Text Mining & NLP: Apply regex, text mining, and fundamental NLP techniques to categorize administrative texts and extract spatial entities. 
- Data Harmonization: Clean and transfer the extracted, geocoded data into our central relational database architecture (PostgreSQL/PostGIS). 

What We Are Looking For 

- Technical Background: Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical industry experience.  
- Core Technical Skills: Solid practical experience in Python, data extraction, API handling, and unstructured format processing (PDF, OCR, JSON). Familiarity with OParl is a strong advantage. 
- Mindset: A proactive problem-solving attitude with an eye for extracting structured truth from bureaucratic texts.  
- Eligibility: Open to local applicants and international candidates (Chancenkarte / Opportunity Card supported).  
- Languages: Professional working proficiency in English (required); fluent or highly proficient German language skills are strictly required to accurately parse and interpret German administrative and legal texts. 

What We Offer 

- Full-Time Permanent Employment: Long-term career stability with clear growth trajectories.  
- Dual Master / Trainee Track Available: Tailored tracks including academic coordination and complete tuition support.  
- Accommodation & Onboarding Package: Structured assistance with local accommodation, official registration, and comprehensive onboarding.  
- Visa & Administrative Backing: Dedicated employer support for Opportunity Card conversions and visa applications.  
- Direct Mentorship: Close collaboration with experienced technical architects and executive leadership.

Location: Germany (Hybrid / Remote options available)

Target Group: Software Engineers, Web Scrapers, OSINT Specialists, Opportunity Card Holders, and Master's Graduates  

About Project IRIS Project IRIS is an applied research and technology initiative dedicated to automated spatial data analysis, infrastructure mapping, and open-source data modeling. Because not all valuable data exists as clean spatial polygons, we build systems that extract hidden knowledge from texts, complex web registries, and unstructured documents. In this role, you will build the autonomous agents that feed our intelligence engine.  

Your Focus & Responsibilities 

- Web Automation: Develop scalable web scrapers and autonomous agents to extract data from unstructured sources (public registers, official announcements, corporate portals). 
- Data Parsing: Parse unstructured web and document data (JSON, XML, HTML, PDF) into clean, relational database structures. 
- Entity Extraction: Apply OCR, regex, and NLP techniques to extract structured entities (addresses, capacities, corporate connections) from dense documents. 
- Pipeline Monitoring: Automate monitoring scripts to continuously feed fresh data into our central PostGIS Data Lake.

- Technical Background: Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Analytics, or equivalent practical industry experience.  
- Core Technical Skills: Proven experience in Web Scraping (Python, Playwright, Scrapy, Selenium, BeautifulSoup) and handling uncooperative web architectures. 
- Mindset: Analytical mindset with a drive for data cleaning, structural modeling, and robust automation.

First Research Article Fellowship Program at the Max Planck Institute for the History

of Science, Berlin

01 September 2027 – 28 February 2028

The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science ( MPIWG) is offering six-month

fellowships for outstanding graduate students enrolled in doctoral programs based at

Asian, African, or Latin American institutions.

Applicants should demonstrate their commitment to a research topic related to the history of

science, technology, and medicine, or science and technology studies, and a need to work

with an international community at the MPIWG in order to prepare and publish their first

single-authored research paper in English.

First Research Article Fellows will be hosted in one of the following departments:

• Artefacts, Action, Knowledge (AAK – Director: Prof. Dr. Dagmar Schäfer)

• Knowledge Systems and Collective Life (KSCL – Director: Prof. Dr. Etienne Benson)

Regular meetings will be held to support both the writing process and academic

development. Fellows are welcome and encouraged to take part in activities offered by the

Institute and by the International Max Planck Research School “Knowledge and Its

Resources” that take place on our campus.

Candidates are expected to have already completed the relevant research for their thesis and

be in a position to devote six months to writing and preparing an article in English for

journal publication. Fellows must remain enrolled in their home institution’s doctoral

program through the end of the advertised fellowship period.

Fellowships are endowed with a monthly stipend according to the guidelines of the Max

Planck Society (https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/projects/first-research-article-

fellowship).

Applicants should submit the following materials in English through our online application

portal:

1. Cover letter explaining how the applicant’s proposed research fits the research

themes of one specific department

1. Official enrollment certificate and confirmation that the applicant will remain

enrolled in an accredited graduate program (PhD) through the end of the

fellowship

1. 500-word description of the dissertation written by the applicant
2. Curriculum vitae (preferably without a photograph) including any publications if

applicable

1. Title, abstract, and outline of article to be completed during the fellowship

(maximum 750 words)

1. English-language writing sample (maximum 8000 words including notes and

bibliography) written by the applicant7. A letter of recommendation from one supervisor

This program is intended to support scholars who wish to improve their academic English.

We encourage you to write your application without the use of AI.

The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science encourages applications from qualified

individuals who belong to groups that are often underrepresented in the workplace due to age,

disability, ethnicity, family status, gender, nationality, race, sex, sexual orientation,

socioeconomic background, or religion.

Please note that only electronic submissions will be accepted. Applications must be

uploaded to the following link on or before 15 January 2027 (23:59 CET):

https://recruitment.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/position/36470793

Finalists may expect a decision by 1 April 2027.

Descriptions of the research projects undertaken by the departments can be found here:

Artifacts, Action, Knowledge (AAK):

https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/department/artifacts-action-knowledge

Knowledge Systems and Collective Life (KSCL):

https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/department/knowledge-systems-collective-life

For further information, please consult the Frequently Asked Questions at the program’s

website: https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/projects/first-research-article-

fellowship.

Help Accelerate Industrial Decarbonization

Join exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.

As our Manufacturing & Industrialisation Engineer, you will help turn our proprietary solar-thermal technology into scalable, repeatable production systems that can be deployed around the world.

This is a hands-on technical role spanning two unique manufacturing environments: component production through external manufacturing partners, and the construction of large solar fields as disciplined, measurable production systems. Working with experienced colleagues, suppliers and project teams, you will contribute from early concepts and specifications through supplier delivery, commissioning, ramp-up and continuous improvement, taking increasing ownership as your capability grows.

Your Impact

Your work will help turn innovative engineering into reliable production and large-scale deployment.

You’ll shape how our technology is manufactured and deployed—from developing production processes and equipment to improving how solar fields are built in the field. Working across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Project Delivery, Construction and HSE, you’ll help create safer, more efficient and repeatable ways of delivering our technology at scale.

What You'll Do

Develop Manufacturing Processes

- Support senior engineers in developing production concepts, equipment specifications, technical evaluations, trials and acceptance plans.
- Take increasing ownership of defined manufacturing processes, tooling packages, supplier actions and site-production workstreams as your capability grows.
- Develop manufacturing processes, machine concepts and equipment specifications for GlassPoint's proprietary concentrating mirrors and film panels.
- Apply DFMA, process capability, standard work, line balancing, cycle-time and capacity analysis to improve safety, quality, output and cost.

Build Tools and Production Systems

- Create clear process documentation, work instructions, layouts, standard work and equipment records.
- Help turn solar-field construction into a repeatable field-production system with defined workflows, work packages, tooling, crew structures and productivity measures.
- Develop or specify production equipment, tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges and handling solutions suited to factories and remote sites.
- Choose the right level of automation - from simple manual aids through mechanised tooling to automated equipment - based on volume, workforce capability, maintainability and economics.

Build Tools and Production Systems

- Work with external equipment builders, integrators and manufacturing partners through technical evaluation, design review, FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up.
- Collect and analyse process data, cycle times, defects, downtime and labour productivity, turning evidence into practical improvement actions.
- Work across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Project Delivery, Construction and HSE, capturing lessons and improving each subsequent deployment.

Commission and Continuously Improve 

- Collect and analyse process data, cycle times, defects, downtime and labour productivity, turning evidence into practical improvement actions.
- Work across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Project Delivery, Construction and HSE, capturing lessons and improving each subsequent deployment.

Who You Are

You’re a practical and curious engineer who wants to understand how products are made, how production systems work and how they can be improved.

You enjoy learning through direct experience in factories, supplier facilities and project sites. You’re reliable, adaptable and comfortable working through engineering problems, analysing data and getting hands-on with production processes and equipment. You’re ready to learn from experienced colleagues and take increasing ownership as your capability grows.

Ideally, you'll bring:

- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Production Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- Typically 10+ years of relevant manufacturing or industrialisation experience, with direct responsibility for production processes, equipment or line deployment.
- A strong record of specifying, procuring, commissioning and ramping production machinery, tooling or automated/semi-automated systems.
- Experience leading engineers, project teams or technical workstreams; formal people-management experience is desirable.
- Deep practical knowledge of DFMA, process capability, tolerancing, error-proofing, line balancing, standard work and continuous improvement.
- Confidence working with equipment builders, system integrators and outsourced manufacturers, including FAT and SAT.
- Experience with large assemblies, modular systems, construction operations or field-deployed production is highly desirable.
- Practical, commercially aware and comfortable making structured decisions with incomplete information.
- Strong English communication skills and willingness to travel internationally, sometimes for extended project phases.

What You'll Find at GlassPoint

- Real ownership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact from day one.
- Exceptional colleagues from diverse disciplines who challenge, support, and learn from each other.
- Complex challenges that require curiosity, collaboration, and innovation.
- An international team united by a shared purpose and ambitious goals.
- The adventure of helping build the future of industrial decarbonization.

We value inclusion and foster a culture of belonging, welcoming team members of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, gender identity, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We have zero tolerance for discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation.
